none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize f(x)+ψ(x) over a convex domain. The function f is globally convex and twice continuously differentiable; ψ is convex on the domain. A global minimizer xstar exists.

problem_class.label: composite
problem_class.details: The smooth component f is accessed through derivatives. The potentially nonsmooth component ψ and domain are accessed through exact regularized model minimization. Extending ψ by +∞ outside the domain gives a proper closed convex function.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Oracle 0 returns ∇f(x) exactly at every queried point, for every call index and seed.

oracle.label: proximal
oracle.details: Oracle 2 exactly minimizes ⟨b,z−c⟩+½⟨z−c,Q(z−c)⟩+(a/3)‖z−c‖³+sψ(z) over the domain. Valid queries require s>0, a≥0, symmetric positive-semidefinite Q, and either a>0 or positive-definite Q. The returned point satisfies the specified variational inequality. No function-value oracle is supplied.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Oracle 1 returns the full exact Hessian ∇²f(x), represented as a continuous linear operator. Its calls are budgeted separately from gradient and model-solver calls.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm. No dimension bound is imposed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The Hessian obeys ‖∇²f(x)−∇²f(y)‖≤H‖x−y‖ globally. Public inputs are E, x0, H>0, R>0, ε>0, and integer m≥1. The feasible starting point satisfies ‖x0−xstar‖≤R. The functions, domain, and minimizer are hidden instance data. No global gradient-Lipschitz bound, bounded domain, or strong convexity is assumed.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output x must satisfy f(x)+ψ(x)−(f(xstar)+ψ(xstar))≤ε.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The returned point must belong to the domain.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: Feasibility and the objective-gap bound hold almost surely under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law, within fixed separate oracle budgets.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: This is standard finite-dimensional composite convex optimization with a Lipschitz Hessian and idealized exact regularized-model solves. Separate oracle budgets specify the complexity accounting.
